t.1.67.1: Those messengers, commanded by Janaka, their mounts wearied, halted on the road for three nights and then entered the city of Ayodhyā.
t.1.67.2: Those messengers, ushered into the royal palace at the king's command, beheld the aged King Daśaratha, who resembled a god.
t.1.67.3: All the messengers, their hands joined in reverence and their fear gone, respectfully addressed the king in words sweet of syllable.
t.1.67.4: The Maithila king Janaka, attended by his sacred agnihotra fires, inquires after your welfare and your unfailing well-being, together with that of your preceptors and family priests.
t.1.67.5: Again and again, O great king, with sweet and affectionate words, Janaka asks after you together with your retinue.
t.1.67.6: Having inquired after your welfare and peace of mind, the Vaideha, lord of Mithilā, with the consent of Kauśika, addressed these words to you.
t.1.67.7: Long ago the vow was made known that my daughter would be won with valor as her bride-price; and the kings, filled with indignation but lacking the strength, were turned away.
t.1.67.8: O king, this daughter of mine has been won by your heroic sons, who came here by chance, led by Viśvāmitra.
t.1.67.9: And that divine bow, O king, was broken in the middle by the great-souled Rāma, O great king, in a vast assembly of people.
t.1.67.10: Sītā, whose bride-price is valour, is to be given by me to this great-souled one. I wish to fulfil my vow; you should grant your permission for that.
t.1.67.11: O great king, come quickly together with your teachers, with your family priest at the head; may good fortune be yours! You ought to see the two Rāghavas.
t.1.67.13: Thus the lord of Videha spoke sweet words, permitted by Viśvāmitra and abiding by the counsel of Śatānanda.
t.1.67.12: O lord of kings, you ought to bring my joy to fulfilment; you too will obtain joy in both your sons.
t.1.67.14: Having heard those words of the messengers, the king, overjoyed, spoke to Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva and to the other ministers.
t.1.67.15: Protected by the son of Kuśika, he who increases the joy of Kausalyā dwells among the Videhas together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa.
t.1.67.17: If the proposal of the great-souled Janaka is pleasing to you, let us go quickly to his city; let there be no lapse of time.
t.1.67.16: Kākutstha's valor has now been witnessed by the great-souled Janaka, and he wishes to make the gift of his daughter to Rāghava.
t.1.67.18: The ministers, together with all the great sages, said, "So be it!" And the king, greatly pleased, said to his ministers, "The journey is tomorrow."
t.1.67.19: And the king's ministers, all endowed with every virtue, highly honoured and full of joy, spent the night there.
